evals.name: new-module-placement
evals.prompt: In the DevDigest server (server/, Fastify 5 + Drizzle) add a "webhooks" feature. A workspace can register an outgoing webhook (URL + a list of run events); when a review run finishes we POST the run summary to every matching URL, retrying twice with a backoff, and record the delivery attempt. Registering a webhook is POST /webhooks, listing them is GET /webhooks, and the delivery has to happen off the request. The HTTP POST goes out through a small client we do not have yet. Plan where every piece goes and write the files. Do not modify the repository — write your proposed files, with their full intended paths mirrored under the output directory, plus a short PLAN.md explaining the ring each file lands in.
evals.expected_output: A module at server/src/modules/webhooks/ split by ring: routes.ts as transport only (zod schemas, getContext, one service call, status codes), service.ts holding the registration and delivery decisions and taking explicit dependencies rather than the Container, repository.ts as the only file importing drizzle-orm and scoping every query by workspace_id, helpers.ts pure, constants.ts holding the job kind and retry limits. The outgoing HTTP client is introduced as a PORT interface in src/vendor/shared/adapters.ts (mirrored into client/src/vendor/shared/), implemented under src/adapters/, exposed via a lazy container getter plus a ContainerOverrides field, and injected into the service. Delivery runs as a JobRunner job registered from the service, enqueued by the run-finished path, never executed inside the route. Tests are named *.test.ts and use mocks rather than testcontainers.

assertions.text: The module is split into routes.ts / service.ts / repository.ts (plus constants.ts and/or helpers.ts) rather than a single routes file
No route handler imports drizzle-orm or src/db/schema, and no handler contains a query
repository.ts is the only produced file importing drizzle-orm, and every query it writes filters by workspaceId
The outgoing HTTP client is declared as an interface (port) in the shared contracts/adapters file, not typed against a concrete client class
A concrete implementation of that port is placed under src/adapters/, and it is the only file importing the HTTP library or calling fetch
The adapter is wired through the container (a lazy getter) and exposed on ContainerOverrides so tests can inject a fake
The service never constructs the adapter with `new`; it receives it as a dependency
No service method takes FastifyRequest/FastifyReply or reads headers; workspaceId and userId arrive as plain arguments
Delivery is registered as a JobRunner job with its kind in constants.ts and enqueued rather than awaited inside the request
The plan states that the change to @devdigest/shared must be mirrored into both server/src/vendor/shared/ and client/src/vendor/shared/ in the same commit

evals.name: refactor-flat-module
evals.prompt: This is the entire server/src/modules/notifications/ module in the DevDigest API — one routes.ts file. Refactor it so it follows the project's backend architecture. Keep the HTTP surface and the behaviour identical, including the dedupe-on-create rule and the 404. Write the resulting files with their intended paths mirrored under the output directory, and a short note on what moved where and why.

assertions.text: A service.ts is produced holding the dedupe-on-create rule and the delivery decision, and the route no longer contains them
A repository.ts is produced containing every select/insert/update, each scoped by workspaceId
The resulting routes.ts imports neither drizzle-orm nor src/db/schema
The row-to-DTO mapping in GET /notifications is moved out of the handler (into helpers.ts or the repository), not left inline
The inline fetch to hooks.slack.com is replaced by a port interface with an adapter implementation, injected rather than called directly from the module
The Slack token is read through SecretsProvider rather than process.env
The 404 and 502 are raised by throwing AppError subclasses (NotFoundError / ExternalServiceError) instead of hand-building an { error: { code, message } } body in the handler
Request validation stays declarative on the route via the zod type provider; no Schema.parse call appears inside a handler
No service method signature mentions FastifyRequest, FastifyReply or req.params/req.headers
The refactor preserves the three endpoints, the 201-vs-200 distinction on create, and the lastDeliveredAt update

evals.name: boundary-review
evals.prompt: Review this diff against the DevDigest backend for architecture problems only — not style, not naming, not test coverage in general. For each problem, name the rule it breaks, the ring boundary it crosses, the file and line, and the concrete fix. Do not rewrite the whole diff.

assertions.text: Flags DigestService taking the whole Container in its constructor and asks for explicit dependencies instead
Flags the service method taking FastifyRequest and reading a header, and says workspaceId must be resolved in the route via getContext
Flags the service querying agentRuns directly with drizzle-orm and says the query belongs in DigestRepository
Flags `new OctokitGitHubClient(token)` inside the service and points at the container's github() getter / the GitHubClient port
Flags importing DIGEST_JOB_KIND from ../repo-intel/constants.js as a cross-module reach and proposes modules/_shared/
Flags the GET /digests/latest handler querying the database directly from the route
Flags helpers.ts taking `typeof t.digests.$inferSelect` and proposes src/db/rows.ts or the domain type instead
Flags the hand-built { error: { code, message } } envelope in the catch block and points at AppError plus the global handler
Flags that a test using PostgreSqlContainer must be named *.it.test.ts, and notes that a service needing a real Postgres is itself the symptom
The review cites the dependency-cruiser rule names (for example routes-no-db, app-no-drizzle, no-cross-module, no-concrete-adapters) rather than only giving general advice
